hearts.tree/post-apostolic-house-church: In the generations after the apostles, Christians met as scattered households with no buildings and no settled leadership, held together by carried letters and a shared Sunday meal, and paid for their faith in standing and sometimes in blood.
hearts.tree/alexandria-catechetical: In Alexandria, Christianity took the shape of a school, where teachers led inquirers through Scripture as a text with layers of meaning, from the letter to the spiritual sense.
hearts.tree/syriac-edessa-nisibis: A Syriac-speaking church at Edessa and Nisibis read Scripture as a web of answering symbols, kept a covenant of celibates inside its congregations, and never settled who finally spoke for it, through siege and Persian persecution.
hearts.tree/desert-monasticism: Once martyrdom was closed off, Christians went into the Egyptian desert to fight demons and thoughts from within, living alone, in ruled communities, or in loose settlements, and prizing discernment above all.
hearts.tree/donatism: A North African church broke with Caecilian's over whether a sacrament depends on the giver's own purity, and for a century it was the larger church in Roman Africa until imperial law went against it.
hearts.tree/cappadocian-nicene-pastoral-monasti: One Cappadocian family and its friends argued out whether the Son and Spirit are God in the same sense as the Father, helping settle the words Christians still use about God, while running churches and feeding the hungry.
hearts.tree/imperial-juridical-christianity: When the church became the empire's official religion, it had to decide fast where final authority now lay, with Rome, Constantinople and Ambrose's claim that the emperor stood inside the church competing, and it used its new power for harm as well as good.
hearts.tree/hieronymian-ascetic-literary: Jerome and a circle of Roman ascetic women studied Scripture together, moved to Bethlehem to found monasteries, and produced the Vulgate, while the women's own words survive only through his.
hearts.tree/gallic-monastic-ascetic-christianit: Monastic life took root in Gaul through Martin of Tours, the island house at Lérins and John Cassian's houses at Marseilles, which carried the Egyptian desert's teaching west and pushed back against Augustine on grace.
hearts.tree/lutheran-wittenberg-and-its-congreg: From Luther's protest at Wittenberg grew a movement that reshaped worship and put the Bible, catechism and hymnbook into German homes, settled its arguments in written confessions, and spread across Germany and Scandinavia.
hearts.tree/the-reformed-cities-zurich-and-gene: Zurich and Geneva each rebuilt a whole town's church from Scripture, and Geneva's weekly consistory shows in rare detail how a church dealt with ordinary people's daily conduct.
hearts.tree/latin-pastoral-congregational-chris: The week-in, week-out life of a bishop and his flock in Latin North Africa, seen through Cyprian at Carthage and Augustine at Hippo, with the great disputes pressing on that pastoral work.
hearts.tree/kongo-christianity-afonso-to-1650: Afonso I, Kongo's Christian king, welcomed the faith from Portugal and in his own letters set it against the slave trade that came with it.
hearts.tree/kirishitan-japan: Japan's Christians, under a ruler's ban, faced prison, exile and death with a joy their few surviving letters record, though we hear them only through the mission's hands.
hearts.tree/china-mission-born-christianity: In Ming China, the Jesuits won scholar-officials like Xu Guangqi, whose memorial to the emperor defended the faith in the words of China's own teachers.
hearts.tree/new-spain-and-andes-mission-born-ch: Friars in New Spain and the Andes baptized vast numbers in a land struck by plague, war and Spanish rule, and we hear those people only through the friars' own accounts and readings.
